Answer: C
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 5b) demonstrates that the opacity indicated by the arrow projects over the posterior ribs and spine, confirming it is located posteriorly. This appearance, combined with its rounded shape on the frontal view, is characteristic of a pseudo-nodule caused by the superimposition of rib structures (rib articulation or crossing) rather than a true intrapulmonary lesion.
